summary: Tested backend and frontend for the security fixes, the manual-customer hours cycle (A), invoices (B), Edit Client (C) and a regression smoke test. Backend: 69 of 69 pass in the security, edit-customer, manual-customer, technicians, connect-auth and stripe-vat suites. test_hours_cycle_invoices.py fails 3 of 17 because of real bugs. The new test_edit_email_invoices.py fails 2 of 2, both real bugs. SECURITY: admin123 now gets 401 and AuxGkyRVwpotScUY works. The 4 locked endpoints return 401 without a token and 403 for a customer token, and work with an admin token. /connect/me no longer contains password_hash. Staff change-password works (401 wrong current password, 400 too short, 200 success, old password then fails). In the UI the Password modal shows the mismatch, wrong-password and success messages; after logout the old password gave 'Credenciais invalidas' and the new one logged in. I reverted the admin password to AuxGkyRVwpotScUY, which is the final password. FEATURE A (UI + DB): I created a client, set start date 2026-08-17 (server date is 2026-10-26), and the period became 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-17 with 0h used. Ajustar -3h set hours_used to 3. I then forced the period to look expired; on the customer dashboard fetch, hours_used went back to exactly 0.0 and the period moved forward exactly one month on day 17. Stripe subscriptions were not touched. FEATURE B: the +Fatura modal created 2 invoices (overdue and paid). The customer's Historico > Faturas section shows both, newest first, with 'Em atraso'/'Pago' badges and the 'Fatura Manual' label. No cross-customer leakage. The Stripe invoice webhook is idempotent. FEATURE C: name and phone edits persist and show in the table. Regression: email-only login for a Stripe customer, admin tabs and stats all work. Bugs found are listed below.

critical.issue: Any UI edit (e.g. phone only) wipes the hours the client has used. The modal always resends subscription_start_date (prefilled from current_period_start), and the backend sets hours_used=0 whenever that field is present. Reproduced: hours_used 2 became 0.0 after a phone-only edit (test_edit_without_date_change_should_not_reset_hours). Fix: only reset hours and recompute the period when the date actually differs from the stored one, or only send the date from the frontend when it was changed.

These are still unauthenticated. Anyone who knows an email can read the full subscription: name, phone, plan, amount, hours and Stripe IDs. This includes manual customers whose login is password-protected, which makes their password protection pointless for this data. Confirmed with curl for cliente.fatura.teste@example.com (200 with full data).

minor.issue: Clients whose start day is 29-31 drift to an earlier day for good. Each new period is computed from the previous period's start instead of the original anchor date, so 31 Jan -> 28 Feb -> 28 Mar -> ... (got 2026-09-28 for an anchor of 31). Fix: store an immutable anchor field (e.g. customer_since) and compute anchor + relativedelta(months=k).

The original 'cliente desde' date is not stored anywhere. The edit modal prefills Data de Inicio with current_period_start (today's cycle start), and the client dashboard 'Desde' shows created_at (26/10/2026) instead of the backdated date (17/08/2026).
Negative or zero amounts are accepted (200). Add Field(gt=0).

Changing a client's email orphans their history. Invoices, work_logs and service_requests are looked up by customer_email and are not updated, so after the change the customer sees 0 invoices. Existing sessions keep the old user_email, so dashboard and change-password stop working until they log in again. Fix: filter customer invoices by subscription_id, and cascade the email change to related records.

No brute-force lockout: login still succeeded after 6 wrong attempts. Staff passwords use unsalted SHA-256 (hash_password); bcrypt is used only for customers. The seed code still falls back to 'admin123'/'tech123' if the environment variables are missing, and the technician still uses the known default 'tech123'.
CORS_ORIGINS='*' together with allow_credentials=True means any origin is reflected back (tested: Origin https://evil.example.com was allowed with credentials). Restrict to explicit origins.
Subscriptions created before this fix still have 30-day periods (cliente.fatura.teste: 10-15 to 11-14), so their anchor will move to day 14 at the next rollover. Consider a one-off migration.

ui_bugs.component: ConnectAdminDashboard Subscricoes table 'Disponiveis' column + Overview 'Subscricoes Ativas' card + Ajustar Horas modal 'Saldo Atual'
ui_bugs.issue: These read sub.hours_available, but the backend never returns that field (0 of 98 subscriptions have it). As a result the table always shows a green '0h', the overview shows 'h disponiveis' and the adjust modal shows 'h' with no number. Compute it on the frontend (hours_included - hours_used) or return it from /connect/admin/subscriptions.

Logout clears localStorage and calls navigate('/connect'), but App.js routes on its own currentPath state (useState(window.location.pathname)), which does not change on router navigation. The URL changes to /connect but the dashboard stays on screen until a full reload. Use window.location.href='/connect' or update currentPath.
'Por:' is always blank. The frontend shows adj.admin_email but the backend stores admin_name.
After a successful change the modal stays open with the success message; it only closes via the X button. Consider auto-closing.

issues: No period/cycle dates (current_period_start/end) are shown, so the admin cannot see a client's cycle in the UI; I had to check it in the DB.

action_items: HIGH: Stop the Editar modal from wiping hours_used. Only treat subscription_start_date as changed when it differs from the stored value (backend), and/or only send it when the admin changed it (frontend).
HIGH: Fix the admin hours_available display (table, overview card, Ajustar Horas 'Saldo Atual'). Compute it as hours_included - hours_used.
HIGH (security): Add authentication to GET /api/customer/subscriptions, /api/customer/subscription/{id} and /api/customer/interventions, or scope them to the logged-in customer's session.
Store an immutable anchor date (customer_since) and compute rollovers from it so day 29-31 clients do not drift. Show it as 'Desde' on the client dashboard and prefill the edit modal with it.
Filter customer invoices by subscription_id (or cascade email changes) so invoice history survives an email edit.
Fix logout in all 3 Connect dashboards (navigate() does not update App.js currentPath).
Security hardening: staff login lockout/rate limiting, bcrypt for staff passwords, remove the 'admin123'/'tech123' fallbacks in startup_seed_accounts, restrict CORS_ORIGINS.
Fix the Ajustes 'Por:' field (admin_email vs admin_name).
Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: it still lists admin123 as the admin password.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3776 lines. Split the connect auth, admin, invoices and stripe webhook code into routers.
edit_manual_customer: hours_reset_needed is triggered by the presence of the field, not by an actual change. This is the root cause of the hours wipe, because the UI always sends the field.

ensure_manual_subscription_period_current writes to the DB during GET requests and runs once per row in the admin list (N updates at most). That is acceptable, but there is no concurrency guard: two parallel requests can both roll over. They are idempotent because the reset is to 0, but intervention hours added between the two could be lost.
complete_intervention calls the rollover and then does $inc on hours_used as two separate operations. If a rollover happens elsewhere between them, the hours could land in the wrong period. Minor.
list_customer_invoices filters by customer_email while admin filters by subscription_id. Inconsistent, and fragile when emails change.

rca of the issue: Hours wipe: openEditClient() prefills subscription_start_date with current_period_start.slice(0,10), and handleEditClient sends the whole form. The backend sees data.subscription_start_date is not None, so it sets hours_reset_needed=True and hours_used=0. Day drift: _advance_period(period_start) chains from the previous, already-clamped period start (Feb 28), so the anchor is permanently reduced. Admin '0h': the JSX reads sub.hours_available, which no endpoint computes for the admin list.
